newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel raises 20 billion yen in samurai issue.
newsitem.headline: Israel raises 20 billion yen in samurai issue.

text.p: Israel raised 20 billion yen ($173.4 million) in its maiden samurai bond offering on Wednesday, the Treasury said.

"The issue attracted very strong demand and because of this the (Treasury) accountant-general agreed to increase the size of the issue from 15 billion yen to 20 billion yen," the Treasury said in a statement.
It said 20 banks participated in the issue. It said the 10-year bonds, which were issued at 99.85 and carry a 3.0 percent coupon, came in at a 48.5-basis-point spread over Japanese government bonds.

"The issue completes the accountant-general's multi-year programme to penetrate the main world capital markets for the purpose of building the financial infrastructure in these markets in advance of the expiry of American loan guarantees," the Treasury said.
The U.S. loan guarantees expire at the end of next year. Israel has already conducted Euro- and Yankee issues.

Daiwa Securities Ltd led the offering after Nomurna Securities Ltd was forced to give up the mandate in the wake of the Japanese government's investigation into Nomura's alleged illegal dealings with corporate racketeers.
